findings.criterion: `upstream_branch_refs` selects remote-tracking refs by excluding the configured ticket event-log branch rather than by matching the local branch name, so the result no longer depends on local and remote branch names agreeing.
findings.detail: The function at src/rebar/_engine_support/commit_impact.py:166-193 still implements the OLD behavior: it gets the current branch name (line 181), builds `suffix = f"/{name}"` (line 192), and returns `[ref for ref in listed.stdout.split() if ref.endswith(suffix)]` (line 193). The fix — excluding the configured tickets branch instead of matching the local branch name — has not been applied to the working tree.

findings.criterion: A new test fixes the fixture on one branch name and the remote commit on another, and asserts the close succeeds; it fails on baseline and passes after the change.
findings.detail: No test for the differing-branch-name close scenario was found. Searched test_completion_gate.py for 'differing_branch', 'branch name differs', 'init -b main' — all returned no matches. The ticket's file_impact declares tests/unit/test_commit_impact.py as a new file, and the plan-review attestation records it as 'dep absent tests/unit/test_commit_impact.py', confirming it does not exist in the working tree.

The test exists at test_completion_gate.py:372-394 and uses `git init -q -b main` for the upstream (line 382) while the rebar_repo fixture uses the system default branch. Since upstream_branch_refs() still filters by local branch name suffix (the bug is unfixed), on systems where the default branch is 'master' the scan returns [] and the test fails — exactly the reproduction described in the ticket.

data.remediation: How to resolve the unmet criteria: use the evidence path that matches each one. For codebase-verifiable work, complete any unfinished work and make its proof discoverable in the repository. For evidence that inherently lives outside the repository, mark the criterion with the exact `[non-codebase]` tag and add a comment to this ticket that documents the concrete artifacts that meet it (commands and their output, links, or the reasoning that ties the evidence to the criterion). The completion verifier reads this ticket's comments, so properly tagged evidence you record there is taken into account on the next verification. An untagged external criterion cannot be satisfied by a ticket comment alone. Then re-verify. Note that a finding reporting a ticket record as absent means it was NOT VISIBLE IN THE TICKET SNAPSHOT THE VERIFIER READ — that snapshot is pinned when the run starts, so a record written after the pin, or not yet committed to the store, reads as missing even though it exists; re-verify after the write lands rather than re-recording evidence you already wrote.
